# Support agent chat

## Problem Statement

The engine has since changed underneath the client in three ways. `hal-engine-single-terminal-frame` (#148) makes `stream_end` the single terminal frame, sent once per accepted message, after a measured probe found an `INVALID_MESSAGE` answer to an unrelated malformed frame landing between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. A client that clears `busy` on any `error` frame drops the typing indicator and unlocks the composer mid-answer. `hal-engine-subprotocol-marker` (#150) stops echoing the client's subprotocol offer and selects only the reserved marker `hal.v1`, so a bare-token offer fails the handshake in both `ws` and Chromium and no customer could connect. The engine's error path now commits the last entry before the `error` frame,…

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the engine half - a sibling issue owns `stream_end` as the single terminal frame and the protocol doc inversion, and another owns committing open entries on every terminal path; what the error frame says and when its notice clears - owned by the Danish failure-messages work, this issue only guarantees `state.error` is still set; redefining `ChatErrorInfo.interrupted`, queued as its own task since both this change and the entry-commit fix invalidate its current computation point; suppressing or restyling an advisory error that arrives mid-healthy-stream - today's behavior of rendering it anyway is kept, any change there is a product question for the failure-messages work; reconnect and resume - the close branch's `busy` clearing is unchanged from `044`. Author: gedaiu
Labels: area:ui, epic:E4, repo:otto, size:XS, type:bug

Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/Otto/issues/191

Part of #1

## Why

`044` clears the client's `busy` flag on `stream_end`, on an `error` frame, or on socket close - a correct reading of the engine's protocol doc as it stood at the time. `139` inverts that contract engine-side after a measured probe found an `INVALID_MESSAGE` answer to a malformed frame landing between two `entry_delta` frames of an otherwise healthy stream: a client that clears `busy` on any `error` frame reads that unrelated frame as "your answer is finished" while the answer is still arriving, dropping the typing indicator and unlocking the composer mid-stream. Under `139` there is now exactly one terminal signal - `stream_end`, sent exactly once per accepted message, error or not - and that issue explicitly supersedes `044`'s client-side rule and queues this issue as the correct…

content.text: {"answer": "No. Under the current design an `error` frame never clears the chat client's `busy` flag. Issue #191 changed this. The earlier rule (#14/044) cleared `busy` on `stream_end`, on an `error` frame, or on socket close. Once the engine made `stream_end` the single terminal frame (#148, issue 139), that rule was wrong. An unrelated `INVALID_MESSAGE` error can arrive between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. Clearing `busy` there drops the typing indicator and unlocks the composer mid-answer. Now `busy` stays true from send until `stream_end` or socket close (FR-013). An `error` frame only sets `state.error`. A `RATE_LIMITED` error leaves `busy` unchanged and changes no entry's `isStreaming` (FR-014). The `isStreaming` sweep moved to `stream_end` and close as backstops (FR-015, FR-016). This relies on `apps/api` pinning HAL Engine 0.3.0, which carries the terminal-frame contract (FR-133).", "sources": ["issue-191 (re-cinq/Otto)", "specs/support-agent-chat/spec.md (FR-013, FR-014, FR-172, Reconciled Decisions #1)", "issue-513", "pull-269"]}
